1360511773686726660 [2021-02-13] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 13 🔁 2
Great conversation I had with @RichDecibels last week about microsolidarity & fluid teams, asking him more about Enspiral since it seems really similar to some of what I'm envisioning with my ideas of a distributed self-energizing meta-team.
https://t.co/OAD2EF6CLF
↓
1360511774701748231 [2021-02-13] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 4
We talk a lot about how to build trust, manage power dynamics, shape membranes, etc.

I like their multi-membrane form, with a core of ~30 you can only join if supermajority approves, who each have individual autonomy to invite ppl to join larger ~200.
https://t.co/gvEjNgZ9ZF
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: 15a/ Membranes. Monists go on about how everything is one, which is true in a sense but also have you noticed that some things are inside and some things are outside? The role of skin, or the walls of a house, or a windshield on a car, is it keeps inside in & outside out.]
↓
1360511775913873409 [2021-02-13] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
One thing I was struck by was him saying that Enspiral neither has agency nor wants anything!

So it's neither necessary nor possible to get the whole group to agree on a direction.

Instead, you go do a thing and invite people into it.
↓
1360511776836603935 [2021-02-13] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 5
I think this is a huge and necessarily about-face from the image of a corporation as almost being a person, with needs, desires, and agency.

At the same time, superorganism metaphors also appeal to me deeply. Maybe teams have agency & wants, but collectives don't? Hmm hmm hmm.
↓
1360511777855840259 [2021-02-13] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
Stoked to hear that since @RichDecibels put out his thinking on https://t.co/FgCmR8stJN he's had >30 communities reach out saying "you put a name to what we're doing!"

Name also enables mutual recognition, though we don't yet know how these entities will relate to each other.
↓

title: "Start businesses together" became a ritual spell
summary:
Qiaochu Yuan kicked this off in Jan 2021 with a deceptively simple “maybe the next phase of the twitter game is we start businesses together,” and the immediate vibe was: yes, but only if it doesn’t turn into an infinite coaching-people-about-coaching black hole. QC’s own hangup was the same—his “commune of dope friends” idea (a consulting/coaching agency with an alexander technique guy, energy worker, business coach, “unlicensed therapist,” etc) felt *ungrounded*, and he explicitly called out the need for an object-level craft (“rationalists should have secret identities”) that actually tests the meta insights. visakanv sharpened the failure mode: no “write ebooks / teach courses about how to write ebooks” ouroboros. QC tried to reframe it as ethical ambition instead of cope: “real rebellion against capitalism is to build wealth with the squad while maintaining impeccable ethical standards.”

The thread’s peak was when people started proposing actual scaffolding, not just vibes. AskYatharth offered the ladder: DM mutuals → calls → tiny projects (website, article) → weekly games → money, with the warning that if small projects don’t feel meaningful you’re not going to pull off the Big Thing. Malcolm Ocean then brought the “grown-up model”: microsolidarity / Enspiral-style coordination—membranes, supermajority-vetted core (~30) plus a larger invited ring (~200), and the key anti-corporate twist: “Enspiral neither has agency nor wants anything… you go do a thing and invite people into it.” QC briefly swerved into a more concrete business-shaped idea—“what if we started a newspaper,” nominating @sashachapin as editor and talking blogs/anthologies as “be the better media.” Then the energy dissipated into assorted “we should do a startup” posts and joke self-awareness about turning success into “Business explaining twitter mutuals how we did it” (nosilverv + exgenesis).

What kept it alive wasn’t one big collective company; it was individuals finally charging money and forming real entities. the_wilderless’ 2022 update is the most honest “execution” moment: multiple people basically staged an intervention—stop giving away draining imaginal/dream guidance for free; treat it as skilled labor, charge real payment, and it’ll be better for both you and clients. Around the same time Danielle Fong posts the most literal “capital formation” beat: she’s doing a seed round for a new energy tech startup and is open to investment from “interesting twitter peeps.” By 2023–2025, Tasshin Fogleman is mostly using QC’s original tweet as a meme/keepsake (“evergreen”), acknowledging the long-game slowness—i.e., the slogan persists even when the group project doesn’t.

Residue: “squad wealth” became a shared incantation *and* a set of recurring guardrails—don’t jump the ladder, don’t go full meta-coach-singularity, build trust via membranes, and if you want the dream to be real you have to price your labor like it is. If you care about internet-friend networks turning into actual livelihood (without becoming scammy course-peddlers), this is basically the origin story of that aspiration—and the clearest map of why it keeps stalling out.
